name: AS301A
description: General purpose externally-compensated operational amplifier, a modern Alfa RPAR clone of the classic National Semiconductor LM301A. Unlike the internally-compensated 741, the user supplies their own frequency-compensation network across the BAL/COMP and COMP pins, trading foolproof stability for tunable bandwidth/stability tradeoffs (overcompensate for margin, or optimize for >10x bandwidth improvement in specific applications). Offers overload protection on input and output, no latch-up with common-mode range exceeded, and low input bias/offset currents suited to integrators, sample-and-holds, and low-frequency waveform generators.

pins.name: BAL/COMP
pins.description: offset null / compensation node; paired with pin 8 (COMP) for the external frequency-compensation capacitor, and with pin 5 (BAL) for offset-null trim

pins.name: BAL
pins.description: offset null balance; used with pin 1 and an external trim pot to null input offset voltage

pins.name: COMP
pins.description: compensation node; paired with pin 1 (BAL/COMP) for the external compensation network (30 pF single-pole cap for unity-gain stability)

TO5-8.notes: Metal-can TO-5 (8-lead), round pin circle package, per the datasheet's page 1 top-view connection diagram (Alfa RPAR AS301A datasheet, 2020 v.3, rev 3). Pin arrangement is identical to the PDIP-8 package below (same numbering, same functions).

PDIP-8.notes: 8-lead 300-mil plastic DIP, per the datasheet's page 1 top-view connection diagram (Alfa RPAR AS301A datasheet, 2020 v.3, rev 3; package dimensional drawing on page 5). Pin arrangement matches the TO5-8 package exactly, both dot/pin-1 referenced top view.

extra.input offset voltage: 2mV typ, 5mV max @ Tamb=25C; 10mV max over full temp range
extra.input offset current: 30nA typ, 200nA max @ Tamb=25C; 300nA max over full temp range
extra.input bias current: 250nA typ, 500nA max @ Tamb=25C; 600nA max over full temp range
extra.large signal voltage gain: 50 V/mV min @ Tamb=25C (Vs=+-15V, RL>=2k, Vout=+-10V, ~93.98dB); 15 V/mV min over full temp range (~83.52dB)
extra.output voltage swing: +-12V min/+-14V typ @ RL=10k; +-11V min/+-13V typ @ RL=2k (Vs=+-15V)
extra.input voltage abs max: +-15V (or supply voltage, whichever is less, for Vs<+-15V)
extra.slew rate: 10V/us typical as a summing amplifier (unity-gain follower, single-pole 30pF compensation)
extra.compensation: externally compensated via pins 1 (BAL/COMP) and 8 (COMP); 30pF single-pole cap is the standard/minimum stable compensation; datasheet gives balancing, two-pole, single-pole, and feedforward compensation topologies with component values

typical_application: General-purpose precision amplification where external compensation is wanted: long-interval integrators/timers, sample-and-hold circuits, low-frequency waveform generators, and summing amplifiers, using the datasheet's balancing, single-pole, two-pole, or feedforward compensation networks to trade stability margin for bandwidth.
gotchas: externally compensated like the original LM301A this clones, not internally compensated like a 741; needs a compensation cap (30pF minimum for unity-gain stability) across pins 1 (BAL/COMP) and 8 (COMP), or it will oscillate
pin 8 is COMP here, not NC as on a 741; despite the superficially similar 8-pin offset-null-at-1&5 / out-at-6 layout, this is not pin-compatible with a 741 socket
offset null uses pins 1 (BAL/COMP, shared with compensation) and 5 (BAL) with an external trim pot, per the balancing-circuit application diagram
guaranteed electrical specs are only over 0C to +70C; -45C and +85C are just 'performance maintained', not full guaranteed-spec range
split supply only; no single-supply operation specified
clone of the National Semiconductor LM301A; same external-compensation philosophy and pinout intent
